title: Ryan McMahon walkoff hit in 11th inning ends wild and strange Yankees victory over Rays - NewsBreak
text: NEW YORK – How many times were the Yankees on the verge of winning or on losing Wednesday night’s game? After being blanked through seven innings by Tampa Bay Rays ’ pitching, the Yankees scored five runs from the eighth inning on, finally winning it in the 11 th at Yankee Stadium. Playing his fifth game as a Yankee, Ryan McMahon delivered a none-out single to deep center that scored automatic runner Jazz Chisholm Jr. from third base, allowing the Yanks to walk off with a 5-4 victory. "It took everybody, right?'' said Cody Bellinger, who contributed an RBI triple in the 10th. "Just a crazy game overall.'' The dramatic and the crazy included three late-game homers, a terrific catch by none other than Jasson Dominguez, an 11th-inning balk and Austin Wells - as the winning run in the ninth - somehow forgetting how many outs there were and getting tagged out, forcing extra innings. But the Rays would ultimately pay for reliever Kevin Kelly's mistake in the 11th. With runners at first and second and McMahon batting, Kelly balked to set the Yanks up for a win that was in and out of their grasp since the home eighth inning. That’s when Trent Grisham belted a game-tying homer off Bryan Baker, followed shortly by Giancarlo Stanton's go-ahead RBI single - only to watch the Rays take a 3-2 lead in the ninth on Josh Lowe’s two-run homer off closer Devin Williams. Anthony Volpe’s one-out homer in the ninth tied it off Rays closer Pete Fairbanks, the subject of trade talk before Thursday’s 7 p.m. MLB deadline – as was Rays’ starter Zack Littell. After tossing five scoreless innings Wednesday, Littell was reportedly traded to the Cincinnati Reds. But the Yanks’ chance at winning it in the ninth ended when Wells forgot how many outs there were on a sacrifice bunt by Grisham (it was nearly a hit) and was tagged out between first and second base. "Just thought there was three outs...very embarrassed and disappointed for sure,'' said Wells, adding he was not deked by any of the Rays' infielders. "I think I was just being an idiot,'' said Wells, who was naturally thrilled by the Yanks' comeback - just their third win this year in nine extra-inning games. The Rays scored once in the 10 th , but left fielder Jasson Dominguez made perhaps his finest catch of the year, banging into the wall on a Jonathan Aranda sac fly, but saving two more runs in the process. "I think they were happier than me,'' Dominguez said of his teammates' reaction, adding that going back aggressively on fly balls is something he's worked on, to overcome his early-season tentative play. "I just need to go get it,'' he said of such plays. Bellinger’s one-out, RBI triple tied it 4-4 in the bottom of the 10 th , but he was stranded there by Stanton and Chisholm Jr. But the Yanks’ fifth reliever, the unsung Tim Hill - who Yanks manager Aaron Boone wanted to avoid using Wednesday, due to workload - held the Rays scoreless in the 11 th and eventually earned the win. In a sharp effort, Yankees starter Will Warren yielded just one run over six innings, matching a season high with 102 pitches in his 23rd start of the year. And he might have had an assist in the 11th. "I may have caused the balk to be called because I was screaming from the dugout,'' said a smiling Warren. One night after committing two throwing errors – but also delivering an RBI single and a long home run in a 7-5 Yanks’ win – Volpe heard the boos again for his eighth inning error. With two out and nobody on base, Volpe charged a softly hit grounder and threw a one-bouncer that first baseman Ben Rice couldn’t handle. Having acknowledged his shortstop is in a defensive slump, “I think Anthony’s super tough. He’s wired for this,’’ said manager Aaron Boone. “He’s got a really high standard for himself. You get in your own way a little bit, especially when you’ve made mistakes,’’ said Boone. “But when you get out there, and it’s game time, go make plays.’’ Boone said his message to Volpe, the 2023 AL Gold Glove Award winner at shortstop, is that “you’re really good at this…he’s a playmaker. “He’s made some mistakes on balls he needs to nail down, but it happens to guys at different points in their career. I feel like his mental toughness…will get him through this.’’ Boone added that he would “continue to pay attention’’ to the Volpe situation defensively, and “make decisions where I see necessary.’’ To date, benching Volpe for the .152-hitting Oswald Peraza isn’t an option. “I have not wanted to do that or decided to do that,’’ Boone said before the game, while acknowledging that “clearly, he’s gone through some struggles here…and not make some plays.’’ This article originally appeared on NorthJersey.com: Ryan McMahon walkoff hit in 11th inning ends wild and strange Yankees victory over Rays
